title: Density Formula for Product Gaussian Integration
statement:
Let $I$ be a finite type, let $E$ be a real normed vector space, let $c:I\to\mathbb R$, and let $v\ge0$ with $v\ne0$. For every function $f:\mathbb R^I\to E$,
\[
\int_{\mathbb R^I}f(z)\,d\Bigl(\bigotimes_{i\in I}N(c_i,v)\Bigr)(z)
=\int_{\mathbb R^I}\Bigl(\prod_{i\in I}q_{c_i,v}(z_i)\Bigr)f(z)\,dz,
\]
where $N(c_i,v)$ is the Gaussian measure with mean $c_i$ and variance parameter $v$, and $q_{c_i,v}$ is its density.
hypotheses_covered: $E$ is a real normed vector space
replaced: Let $I$ be a finite set, $c\in\mathbb R^I$, $v>0$, and $\mu_{c,v}=\bigotimes_{i\in I}N(c_i,v)$. For a real normed vector space $E$ and any $f:\mathbb R^I\to E$, $\int f\,d\mu_{c,v}=\int_{\mathbb R^I}(\prod_i p_v(c_i,z_i))f(z)\,dz$, where $p_v$ is the scalar Gaussian density and nonintegrable integrals on either side are assigned zero.
